a.summary: The sibling single-table overload `createTx(List, int, AccountMeta[], AddressLookupTable)` compacts the caller's `sortedAccounts` in place exactly as the newly documented overload, but carries no javadoc — and the documented overload delegates to it for the one-table case.
a.failure_scenario: A consumer builds one v0-sorted array `[payer, W1, W2, P(invoked,read), R1(read)]` and reuses it for two transactions. Call 1: `createTx(ixs, len, sorted, tableA)` where tableA holds W2 — the loop at 298-306 leaves the array as `[payer, W1, P, R1, W2]`. Call 2: `createTx(ixs, len, sorted, tableB)` where tableB holds R1 instead — the loop now walks the already-permuted array and produces an included front of `[payer, W1, P, W2]` with `numReadonlyUnsignedAccounts = 1`. The runtime reads the header as "the last unsigned account is readonly", so W2 (a real writable account) is serialized readonly and P (a program account) is serialized writable. The transaction serializes without error and mis-privileges accounts. Nothing at the declaration warns the caller; the documented sibling at line 439 says "Pass a clone to preserve the input array's order" and this one says nothing.

b.summary: The sibling public overload `createTx(List, int, AccountMeta[], AddressLookupTable)` compacts the caller's array in place exactly as the newly documented overload does, but the delta leaves it with no javadoc at all.
b.failure_scenario: A consumer builds `sortedAccounts` once and calls `Transaction.createTx(instructions, len, sortedAccounts, lookupTable)` (line 266) for a single table. The loop at lines 298-306 rotates included accounts to the front, so `sortedAccounts` comes back reordered. Reading only the declarations, the consumer sees the warning on the four-table overload (lines 435-438) and nothing on this one, concludes this overload is safe, and reuses the array — for a second `createTx` call, or to resolve `sortedAccounts[i]` by an index computed before the call — and silently gets the wrong account.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
